title: Human Body & Medicine
description: 36 original questions on organs, bones, blood types, senses, and medical milestones with vector anatomy SVGs.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which twisted ladder-shaped molecule carries genetic instructions in living organisms, as illustrated here?
questions.explanation: DNA's double-helix structure was famously modeled in 1953 using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data.

questions.prompt: Which pair of spongy respiratory organs illustrated here exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide with the blood?
questions.explanation: The lungs contain hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli.

questions.prompt: Which colored ring-shaped muscle in the eye illustrated here controls the size of the pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris expands or contracts to regulate how much light enters the pupil.

questions.prompt: Which central organ illustrated here serves as the control center of the human nervous system?
questions.explanation: The adult human brain contains roughly 86 billion neurons.

questions.prompt: How many bones are in a typical adult human skeleton?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with about 270 bones, many of which fuse together by adulthood.

questions.prompt: What is the largest internal organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver weighs about 1.5 kg and performs over 500 metabolic functions.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body overall?
questions.explanation: Skin accounts for roughly 15% of total adult body weight.

questions.prompt: Which blood type is known as the universal red blood cell donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative red cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens, minimizing transfusion reactions.

questions.prompt: Which blood type is known as the universal red blood cell recipient?
questions.explanation: AB-positive individuals have no anti-A, anti-B, or anti-Rh antibodies.

questions.prompt: What is the longest and strongest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) supports the weight of the body during standing and walking.

questions.prompt: Where are the three smallest bones in the human body located?
questions.explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes (ossicles) transmit sound vibrations in the middle ear.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: Two upper atria receive blood and two lower ventricles pump blood out.

questions.prompt: Which protein in red blood cells binds oxygen and gives blood its red color?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin contains iron atoms that reversibly bind oxygen in the lungs.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces insulin to regulate blood sugar levels?
questions.explanation: Beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans secrete insulin.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is primarily produced when human skin is exposed to UVB sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption and bone health.

questions.prompt: Who discovered penicillin, the world's first widely used antibiotic, in 1928?
questions.explanation: Fleming noticed a Penicillium mold killing Staphylococcus bacteria on a petri dish.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain is primarily responsible for balance and coordinating smooth movement?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum sits at the back of the skull beneath the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood AWAY from the heart?
questions.explanation: Most arteries carry oxygen-rich blood (except the pulmonary artery).

questions.prompt: What is the normal resting body temperature of a healthy human in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Normal human core temperature averages around 36.5°C–37.2°C (98.6°F).

questions.prompt: Which hard outer layer of human teeth is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.explanation: Tooth enamel is over 95% mineral (hydroxyapatite).

questions.prompt: Which doctor pioneered the smallpox vaccine in 1796 using cowpox?
questions.explanation: The word 'vaccine' derives from the Latin 'vacca' (cow).

questions.prompt: Which cells in the human immune system are primarily responsible for fighting infections?
questions.explanation: Leukocytes include neutrophils, lymphocytes, and macrophages.

questions.prompt: Which blood components help blood clot to stop bleeding?
questions.explanation: Platelets clump together at wound sites to form a protective plug.

questions.prompt: What is the medical name for the collarbone?
questions.explanation: The clavicle connects the sternum (breastbone) to the shoulder blade.

questions.prompt: What is the medical name for the kneecap?
questions.explanation: The patella is the largest sesamoid bone in the human body.

questions.prompt: Which organ filters waste products from the blood to produce urine?
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about one million tiny filtering units called nephrons.

questions.prompt: Which deficiency causes scurvy, historically common among sailors on long voyages?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is required for collagen synthesis.

questions.prompt: Which structure in the brain plays a vital role in forming new long-term memories?
questions.explanation: Named for its seahorse shape, the hippocampus consolidates short-term into long-term memory.

questions.prompt: Which scientist developed the first successful inactivated polio vaccine in 1955?
questions.explanation: Salk famously chose not to patent the polio vaccine so it could be distributed worldwide.

questions.prompt: Which valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle of the heart?
questions.explanation: Also called the bicuspid valve, it prevents backflow into the left atrium.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the wave-like muscle contractions that move food down the esophagus?
questions.explanation: Peristalsis pushes food along the digestive tract even if you swallow upside down.

questions.prompt: Which hormone is commonly known as the 'fight-or-flight' hormone released by the adrenal glands?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline increases heart rate, blood flow to muscles, and alertness.

questions.prompt: Which hormone secreted by the pineal gland regulates the body's sleep-wake cycle?
questions.explanation: Melatonin levels rise in darkness to signal the body that it is time to sleep.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the tiny finger-like projections in the small intestine that absorb nutrients?
questions.explanation: Villi dramatically increase the internal surface area of the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which nerve transmits visual information from the retina to the brain?
questions.explanation: The optic nerve consists of over a million nerve fibers.

questions.prompt: What is the longest and thickest nerve in the human body, running from the lower back down each leg?
questions.explanation: Compression of the sciatic nerve causes the radiating pain known as sciatica.
